headline: Sawtooth National Forest and Resort Access
reservation: Day use generally requires no permit, but overnight stays in the Sawtooth Wilderness require self-registration at trailheads. Peak winter and summer resort lodging should be booked months in advance; always check the official US Forest Service site for current fire restrictions and area closures.

days.title: High Desert Valleys and Nordic History
days.start: Suggested: 9 AM from Ketchum Town Square

stops.name: Sun Valley Lodge
stops.detail: Visit the historic site of the first destination ski resort in America and its iconic skating rink.

stops.name: Wood River Trail
stops.detail: A multi-use paved path connecting the valley towns with gentle grades and river views.

days.driving: Allow 20 minutes for local transfers; conditions vary.
days.note: The Wood River Trail is cleared in winter for walking and Nordic skiing.

days.title: Alpine Lakes and Sawtooth Vistas

stops.name: Galena Lodge
stops.detail: A historic day lodge serving as a hub for extensive hiking and cross-country ski trails.

stops.name: Boulder Mountains
stops.detail: Explore the rugged peaks flanking the eastern side of the valley for high-altitude solitude.

days.driving: Allow 1 hour for mountain road driving; conditions vary.
days.note: Snow can linger on high-altitude trails through late June.

days.title: River Canyons and Cultural Heritage

stops.name: Big Wood River
stops.detail: A world-class fly fishing destination known for its clear water and scenic banks.

stops.name: Proctor Mountain
stops.detail: Site of the world's first chairlift, offering a moderate hike with panoramic valley views.

days.driving: Allow 40 minutes for valley transit; conditions vary.
days.note: River levels rise significantly during spring runoff in May and June.

intel.title: Ketchum Downtown Access
intel.text: Public parking in downtown Ketchum is time-limited; use the peripheral lots for longer hikes. Trailhead parking at popular spots like Adam's Gulch fills by early morning in July.

intel.title: Backcountry Dead Zones
intel.text: Cell service drops immediately north of Galena Summit. Carry a satellite communication device if venturing deep into the Sawtooth Wilderness.

intel.title: Last Service Northbound
intel.text: Ketchum is the last reliable source for fuel and full services before heading north over Galena Summit toward Stanley. Check your gauge before entering the National Recreation Area.

intel.title: Wildlife Migration
intel.text: Autumn visitors should watch for the Trailing of the Sheep festival, which can temporarily close local roads. Early morning is the best time to spot elk in the lower meadows.

intel.title: Forest Road Conditions
intel.text: Many secondary forest roads remain closed by snow until late spring. Check the Sawtooth National Forest 'Motor Vehicle Use Map' for official seasonal openings.

plan.arrival: Fly into SUN airport, rent a vehicle in Hailey, and drive 20 minutes north to Ketchum for lodging check-in.
plan.vehicle: High-clearance vehicles are recommended for forest service roads; check rental contracts for unpaved road restrictions.
plan.goldenHour: Bald Mountain provides a dramatic backdrop for sunset photography from the White Clouds loop.
